public_rationale: This is a sweeping summary of several broad trends rather than one checkable claim. The cyberscam part can be measured, and FBI-based data show large AI-linked scam losses in 2025, which fits his view. But 'enshittification of the web' has no agreed measure, 'mass spread of misinformation' has no threshold, and 'and so on' leaves the list open. Any verdict on 'it's all happening' would rest on a reading he did not supply. Whether he made the warnings years ago is a fact about his own newsletter, which we do not use as evidence that he was right.
limitations: Only the cyberscam part was looked at in detail.
The evidence item was published after the post and is context only.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The harms Marcus warned about years ago (enshittification of the web, mass misinformation, more cyberscams) are now all happening.

statement.excerpt: In this newsletter years ago, I warned about the enshittification of the web, the mass spread of misinformation, increases in cyberscams, and so on, and it’s all happening.
statement.document_title: A few dark words about chatbots and death

our_interpretation: The claim bundles three or more broad trends plus an open-ended 'and so on'. Only the cyberscam part has an ordinary measurable reading (reported scam losses rising). 'Enshittification of the web' is a loose, value-laden term with no agreed measure, and 'mass spread of misinformation' has no stated threshold or baseline.
Whether Marcus made the warnings is a fact about his own writing, which cannot serve as evidence that he was right.
criteria.support_condition: Measurable evidence that all named harms (web quality decline, mass misinformation, rising cyberscams) are occurring in the period up to January 2026.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Measurable evidence that one or more named harms is not occurring, e.g. falling scam losses or improving web quality on an agreed metric.

evidence.excerpt: The 2025 Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Internet Crime Report shows that Americans reported $893,346,472 in AI‑related scam losses.
evidence.explanation: Shows AI-linked scams are substantial, which fits the cyberscam part. It says nothing about web quality or misinformation, and it was published after the post.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A narrower restatement with named metrics, for example year-over-year scam losses, the share of AI-generated web content, or rates of false claims, each with a baseline.
